title: Direct-image base change under the geometric-stalk condition
statement:
Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme], and work with algebraic spaces over $S$ and their small etale structure sheaves [def-trf-algebraic-space], in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Use the unbounded module derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the canonical tensor pullback and direct image [def-trf-space-etale-module-functors], their total derived functors computed by K-flat resolutions with flat terms and K-injective resolutions, and K-flat derived tensor product. Write $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_Z)$ for objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y'\to Y$ be morphisms, and set $X'=X\times_Y Y'$ with projections $g':X'\to X$ and $f':X'\to Y'$. For a geometric point $\bar x':\operatorname{Spec}\Omega\to X'$ with $\Omega$ algebraically closed, write $\bar x=g'\bar x'$, $\bar y'=f'\bar x'$, $\bar y=f\bar x$, and put $R=\mathcal O_{Y,\bar y}$, $A=\mathcal O_{X,\bar x}$, $B=\mathcal O_{Y',\bar y'}$, $C=\mathcal O_{X',\bar x'}$, $D=A\otimes_R B$. The stalks are colimits over pointed etale scheme neighbourhoods, and $D\to C$ is induced by the projection stalk maps. For $K\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$, $K'\in D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_{X'})$ and $\phi:L(g')^*K\to K'$, define the stalk comparison $\beta^i_{\phi,\bar x'}$ to be
$$H^i(K_{\bar x}\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B)\otimes_D C\longrightarrow H^i(K'_{\bar x'}).$$
Here the arrow is induced by $K_{\bar x}\otimes_R^{\mathbf L}B\to K_{\bar x}\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}C\simeq(L(g')^*K)_{\bar x'}\xrightarrow{\phi_{\bar x'}}K'_{\bar x'}$, extended $C$-linearly on cohomology. Assume $f$ is quasi-compact and quasi-separated (tested on etale scheme charts), and that $\beta^i_{\phi,\bar x'}$ is an isomorphism for every geometric $\bar x'$ and every $i\in\mathbf Z$. Then the composition
$$Lg^*Rf_*K\xrightarrow{\mathrm{Ex}}Rf'_*L(g')^*K\xrightarrow{Rf'_*(\phi)}Rf'_*K'$$
is an isomorphism in $D(\mathcal O_{Y'})$. Here $\mathrm{Ex}$ is the adjunction-mate map: its adjoint is $L(f')^*Lg^*Rf_*K\simeq L(g')^*Lf^*Rf_*K\to L(g')^*K$, with the last arrow the pullback of the counit of $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$. No Tor-independence, properness or boundedness is required.

proof.text: Use etale chart calculus to restrict first to affine etale charts $V\to Y$, then to affine etale charts $V'\to Y'\times_YV$. These cover the two bases by the algebraic-space atlas definition and the fibre-product covering lemma. Under the restriction isomorphisms, the exchange is still the stated mate: pullback composition respects units and counits. The stalk-condition chart lemma preserves the hypothesis. Thus it suffices to prove the assertion when $Y,Y'$ are affine. Indeed exact restriction commutes with cohomology, and a cohomology sheaf vanishing on a covering is zero by the sheaf axiom. The restricted $f$ is qcqs by the chart-tested hypothesis, so its source $X$ is qcqs over the affine base.

source.place: Tag 0DKH (lemma-single-complex-base-change), etale localization in the opening paragraph

proof.text: For each qcqs etale algebraic space $T\to X$, put $T'=T\times_YY'$ and let $P(T)$ say that the canonical composite $\gamma_T:Lg^*R(T\to Y)_*(K|_T)\to R(T'\to Y')_*(K'|_{T'})$ is invertible. Use the restricted coefficient map, with the canonical pullback composition comparisons. The stalk-condition chart lemma supplies the same hypothesis on every such restriction. We verify the affine and distinguished-square premises of the algebraic-space induction principle.

source.place: Tag 0DKH (lemma-single-complex-base-change), induction setup in the opening paragraph

proof.text: If $T$ is affine, then $T,Y,Y',T'$ are schemes. Transport the complexes and coefficient map through the etale–Zariski equivalence. Its pullback and pushforward comparisons respect composition, so adjunction uniqueness identifies the transported exchange with the scheme mate. The chart lemma gives exactly the ordinary stalk hypothesis. Apply the existing scheme single-complex qcqs criterion; $T\to Y$ is a morphism of affines and hence qcqs. Transporting its isomorphism back proves $P(T)$.

For an elementary distinguished square $(U\subset W,V\to W)$ in the induction principle, apply the relative Mayer–Vietoris exchange lemma to $K|_W$, $K'|_{W'}$, and the restricted coefficient map. It gives a morphism of distinguished triangles with components $\gamma_W$, $\gamma_U\oplus\gamma_V$, $\gamma_{U\times_WV}$. The latter two are invertible by the three induction assumptions (the inverse of a direct sum is the direct sum of the inverses). The two-out-of-three lemma for triangle morphisms proves $P(W)$.

source.place: Tag 0DKH (lemma-single-complex-base-change), induction step and displayed triangle diagram

proof.text: The algebraic-space induction principle now gives $P(X)$, whose arrow is the required composite, with the identity restrictions and unital composition comparisons. Undo the etale restrictions of Step 1; its cohomology sheaves are isomorphisms on a covering and therefore everywhere. This proves the claimed isomorphism in the unbounded derived category.
